script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

Title: The Weight of Forgiveness

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

A quaint, sunlit coffee shop. A place of community, comfort, and connection. JANE (35), an unassuming woman, sits alone at a table, her eyes fixed on a worn photograph.

Waitress brings her latte.

WAITRESS
(cheerfully)
Here you go, Jane. How's your day been?

JANE
(looking up)
Fine, thank you. Just lost in thought.

WAITRESS
(nods)
You know, this place is full of second chances. Maybe you'll find yours today.

INT. COURTROOM - DAY

Jane sits in a cold, sterile courtroom, her eyes fixed on the defendant's chair. A young man, MIKE (25), sits nervously, looking at the jury. His lawyer, MRS. GREENE (50), a seasoned professional, whispers reassuringly.

JUDGE
(gavel)
Court is now in session. We have a case of negligence and wrongful death. The plaintiff, Jane Doe, alleges that the defendant, Michael Johnson, was driving under the influence of alcohol at the time of the accident, resulting in the death of her husband. How do you plead, Mr. Johnson?

MIKE
(whispers to his lawyer)
Not guilty.

INT. JANE'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jane sits alone in her dimly lit living room, the photograph still clutched in her hands. A knock on the door startles her. It's MIKE.

MIKE
(hesitantly)
I wanted to speak with you, Jane. About what happened.

JANE
(angrily)
There's nothing to say. You took something from me that I can never get back.

MIKE
(tearfully)
I know. I carry that burden every day. I was drunk that night, I made a mistake. But I'm sober now. I've changed. I want to make amends.

Jane looks at him for a long moment before speaking.

JANE
(sighs)
What do you want from me?

MIKE
(kneels)
I want to help you. I want to make it right. Whatever you need, I'll do it.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane sits at her usual table, the photograph long since put away. Mike enters, carrying a bouquet of flowers.

MIKE
(nervously)
Can I join you?

JANE
(looks up, surprised)
(pauses)
Yes.

They sit in silence for a moment, the weight of their past heavy between them.

MIKE
(tentatively)
Jane, I know I can't bring your husband back. But I can help you move forward. I can be there for you, support you.

JANE
(sighs)
I don't know, Mike. I don't know if I'm ready for that.

MIKE
(reaches across the table)
I understand if you're not. But I'll be here, whenever you are.

INT. COURTROOM - DAY

The trial concludes with a guilty verdict, but the judge grants Mike a chance at redemption.

JUDGE
(gavel)
Mr. Johnson, you will serve five years probation, perform 500 hours of community service, and undergo regular alcohol counseling. This is your second chance. Do not waste it.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jane sits at her table, watching Mike as he enters, carrying a tray of coffees. He sets one down in front of her before joining her at the table.

MIKE
(smiling)
Morning coffee?

JANE
(smiling back)
Always.

They sit in comfortable silence as the sun streams through the windows, casting dappled light on their table. The weight of forgiveness, heavy but lifting, hangs between them.

FADE OUT.

End screenplay.
